report:
**Conclusion:** Contrary to your initial expectation, scientific evidence indicates that **yes**, olive leaf extract can help reduce high blood pressure.

**Key Evidence:**

* **Clinical Trials:** A double-blind, randomized clinical trial in patients with stage-1 hypertension found that olive leaf extract effectively reduced blood pressure, demonstrating anti-hypertensive effects comparable to the prescription medication Captopril (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21036583/).
* **Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses:** Comprehensive reviews of clinical trials show that olive leaf extract supplementation leads to a statistically significant lowering of systolic blood pressure (https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/80445/ ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13098-022-00920-y).
* **Biological Mechanism:** The primary active compound in olive leaf extract, oleuropein, is believed to lower blood pressure by inhibiting angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) and decreasing the constriction of blood vessels (https://naturalhealthresearch.org/olive-leaf-lowers-blood-pressure/).

While these findings support its efficacy, individuals considering olive leaf extract for blood pressure management should consult a healthcare provider to ensure safety and prevent potential drug interactions.
